name: Steve Scalise
role: U.S. representative from Louisiana (2008–present); House majority leader since 2023
summary: Scalise supports lower taxes, business deregulation, fossil-fuel development and conditional welfare benefits. He opposes abortion and same-sex marriage, champions gun rights and border enforcement, and advocates military superiority and security surveillance.

universal-healthcare.rationale: Scalise says Democrats want all Americans on government-run health care and that it has "failed in every country it's been tried".

raise-minimum-wage.rationale: He voted against the Raise the Wage Act in 2019 (House passage 231-199); no statement of his own on the wage level was found.

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: He demands permanent Trump-era tax rates and opposes allowing higher individual rates.

regulate-corporations.rationale: He advocates removing business and construction regulations to lower costs and stimulate jobs.

cut-welfare.rationale: He argues benefits for able-bodied nonworkers encourage idleness and should be withdrawn.

surveillance-ok.rationale: He advocates renewing FISA authorities specifically to prevent terrorist attacks.

legalize-drugs.rationale: He endorses permanent Schedule I prohibition of fentanyl-related substances.

limit-guns.rationale: He rejects additional gun restrictions and defends broad Second Amendment rights.

empower-police-military.rationale: He demands greater defense funding and replenishment of advanced military equipment.

decide-locally.rationale: He says communities, rather than Washington, should decide whether to host data centers.

rehabilitation.rationale: He supported the First Step Act’s reintegration, good-conduct credits and prison reforms.

same-sex-marriage.rationale: He authored Louisiana’s opposite-sex-only marriage amendment and later opposed federal marriage recognition.

abortion-legal.rationale: He celebrates overturning Roe and demands protection for every unborn child.

free-trade.rationale: In 2018 he said "I don't want tariffs. I want a free trade environment", and in 2025 he said the aim of tariff talks is to lower tariffs on both sides, ideally to zero; he voted for the USMCA and the Colombia trade agreement.

nation-first.rationale: He explicitly endorses putting American workers and innovators first in trade negotiations.

open-borders.rationale: He champions a fortified border wall and stronger Border Patrol enforcement.

limit-growth.rationale: He condemns climate policies that would reduce manufacturing and damage economic activity.

drastic-climate-action.rationale: He rejects compulsory zero-emission policies and describes Paris-style targets as economically destructive.

expand-nuclear.rationale: He supports nuclear baseload as a necessary alternative to reliance on wind and solar alone.

tariffs-protect-industry.rationale: He praises reciprocal tariffs as protecting American workers against unfair foreign practices.

military-superiority.rationale: He explicitly says America must maintain the world’s strongest armed forces.

jewish-state-israel.rationale: In a leadership statement he affirmed "ironclad support for Israel as it fights for its very right to exist".

school-vouchers.rationale: He champions a nationwide school-choice tax credit supporting low-income pupils’ alternative schooling.

work-for-welfare.rationale: He explicitly demands work requirements for able-bodied adults receiving Medicaid and other welfare.

expand-fossil-fuels.rationale: He demands expanded production from Alaska to the Gulf and removal of drilling restrictions.

separated-powers.rationale: He welcomed Loper Bright because Chevron "upended the separation of powers between our three branches" and the ruling "restores the balance outlined by the Founders".

no-bailouts.rationale: He voted no on the 2008 Emergency Economic Stabilization Act (the bank bailout), and on its rule.

restrict-foreign-funding.rationale: His endorsed agenda restricts foreign university contracts and demands disclosure of foreign gifts.

non-intervention.rationale: He strongly endorses attacks on Iran to destroy nuclear capabilities and deter threats.

gender-identity-recognition.rationale: He voted against the Equality Act in 2019 and says women's sports should be reserved for biological women.

ban-nda-harassment.rationale: He voted for the 2022 Ending Forced Arbitration of Sexual Assault and Sexual Harassment Act and for the Speak Out Act.

open-lgbt-military-service.rationale: Only a Wikipedia summary was cited; no source of the person's own words or record was reached.

abolish-police-prisons.rationale: He explicitly rejects proposals to abolish police forces and prisons.

foreign-residents-local-vote.rationale: He says it "shouldn't be the case" that foreign embassy staff can vote in D.C. elections and backed the House bill to stop noncitizens voting there.

sex-socially-constructed.rationale: He endorses defining sex through birth genetics for school athletic eligibility.

defensive-wars-only.rationale: He supports preventive strikes against Iran’s nuclear programme, beyond repelling an ongoing invasion.

pollution-taxes.rationale: He endorses repealing the federal methane-emissions fee on petroleum and gas facilities.

collective-bargaining.rationale: He opposed the PRO Act but endorsed restoring collective-bargaining rights for Washington police; his record differs by sector.

fiscal-rules-binding.rationale: He voted for the 2011 balanced budget amendment and the Cut, Cap and Balance Act, and for caps in the Limit, Save, Grow Act.

student-debt-relief.rationale: In a statement he issued as a leader he called Biden's student loan relief a "giveaway to the wealthy" and the Limit, Save, Grow Act stops it.

public-service-media.rationale: He celebrates his rescission of federal funding for the Corporation for Public Broadcasting.

mandatory-sentences.rationale: He criticised the D.C. bill that removed mandatory minimum sentences for violent crimes and supported the House bill to block it.

voter-id.rationale: He explicitly demands photo identification to protect the integrity of elections.

international-criminal-courts.rationale: He endorses sanctions against ICC efforts to prosecute protected American and allied officials.

close-ties-china.rationale: He frames China as an AI competitor America must defeat, rather than a preferred economic partner.

notes:
Whole-career review includes Louisiana marriage legislation, congressional votes and official statements through September 2026. Full official speech and interview texts were downloaded and searched. His support for rehabilitative First Step Act reforms qualifies a purely punitive description. Unlawful-entry restrictions do not establish a desired reduction of lawful immigration or exclusion of all lawful immigrants from welfare. Climate criticism is attributed to him without endorsing its scientific claims. The 2002 EURO appearance and subsequent apology were reviewed; attendance alone does not establish racial segregation or hereditary-race beliefs. His 2020 election objections likewise do not establish opposition to competitive elections as a principle. No inference from party or religious identity. AI infrastructure advocacy does not establish algorithmic government, and gender-specific sports rules do not establish a general theory of gender. Early-2023 agenda letter was dated from its contents rather than recent search indexing.

Merged with an independent claude-sonnet-5-5 audit: 12 answers taken from it, 18 agreed, 0 conflicts settled by the integrator.

claude-sonnet-5-5 notes: Independent second pass. Searched his House press releases (488 pages, mostly 2023-2026, from scalise.house.gov), the Majority Leader site, 2016-2018 CNN and NPR interviews (MediaSum) and his roll-call votes (Voteview). Themes searched: economy, society, liberty, world, government, ecology, technology (AI and data centres gave only a local-decision remark, left null), means (nothing on political violence found), culture. The Alex Jones Show corpus had only mentions of him, no guest segments. Trade: 2018 anti-tariff words and 2025 support for tariffs as leverage are recorded as 0 on tariffs. Several answers rest on votes only (medium). Blocked: Britannica and Congress.gov member pages (bot wall).
